column3: Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew describes the people as “great and tall”; BSB says “strong and tall.”
Close to the Hebrew.
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew joins righteousness and uprightness with “and,” explicitly repeats the LORD’s name before the oath, and says “the word”; BSB uses “or,” a pronoun, and “the promise.”
Close to the Hebrew.
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew explicitly names the LORD twice; BSB uses “He” for the second occurrence.
The Hebrew uses the image of cutting the covenant; BSB says “made” the covenant.
The Hebrew says the words were “on them” and repeats the root for speaking in “the words” and “spoke”; BSB incorporates the words into the description of the inscription.
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew states that they turned aside quickly; BSB gives this statement the exclamatory form “How quickly.”
The Hebrew has both “said” and “saying” and uses “behold”; BSB has a single “said” and “indeed.”
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew says “my two hands”; BSB says “my hands.”
The Hebrew includes “behold” after “I saw”; BSB expresses this as “I saw how.”
The Hebrew explicitly says “my two hands”; BSB says “my hands.”
The Hebrew says “evil in the eyes of the LORD”; BSB uses “evil in the sight of the LORD.”
Close to the Hebrew.
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew calls the calf “your sin” and repeats “its dust”; BSB says “that sinful thing” and refers to casting “it” into the stream.
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew uses “the mouth of the LORD” and “His voice”; BSB says “the command of the LORD” and “obeyed Him.”
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew repeats the verb for falling down in a relative clause; BSB states the action once.
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew separately lists the people’s stubbornness, wickedness, and sin; BSB combines the final two as “the wickedness of their sin.”
The Hebrew makes “the land” the subject of saying; BSB makes its inhabitants explicit with “those in the land.”
Close to the Hebrew.
